The theorem states that a distributed data store cannot simultaneously provide all three guarantees. The combinations: CA (not partition tolerant; if partition occurs, must sacrifice availability or consistency; rarely used), CP (consistency and partition tolerance; system may become unavailable when partition occurs), AP (availability and partition tolerance; system may return inconsistent data during partition). Provide real-world systems: CA: some relational databases with master-master replication? But need 3 examples. CP: some NoSQL like MongoDB (consistency oriented), HBase, Zookeeper? AP: Cassandra (tunable consistency), DynamoDB, CouchDB. Provide 3 each.

Also provide mathematical formal definition: define a distributed system as a set of nodes communicating over network; define properties: Safety (consistency) as "any read returns most recent write or some invariant", Liveness (availability) as "every request receives a response", Partition tolerance as "system continues to operate despite network partitions". Formal definitions using linearizability, etc.

We can also mention that CAP is about a trade-off at the time of partition; not a binary but a continuum; some systems can be tuned.
